title: Alien Gate HUD lower edge is missing
symptom: The lower pixels of the elevated gameplay HUD are absent, removing the bottoms of labels such as SHIELD. The cause could be source drawing, transfer, origin, clipping, or plane composition; it is not yet classified as a layering defect.
expected: Real-hardware footage shows authored windowboxed gameplay with a bottom black bar and a complete elevated HUD. Projectile sprites may cross the playfield boundary, but the background and enemy face remain below the HUD.
revalidation_reason: The missing HUD pixels were manually reproduced on the current diagnostic working tree. The real-hardware reference establishes presentation expectations but does not identify the faulty emulation stage.

scenario.dvc: vmpega present but title uses base graphics
input_events: pause to inspect HUD and sprite boundaries

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The missing HUD edge may originate in guest drawing or transfer, MCD212 line origin/clipping, plane composition, or final aperture presentation. No stage is preferred until provenance is captured.
supporting_evidence: The current screenshot lacks the lower portions of HUD lettering.
The user-supplied real-console video shows the full HUD, authored windowboxing and bottom bar, and projectile sprites crossing outside the playfield.
contradicting_evidence: No current individual-plane, composed-raster, or frontend-stage capture exists.
The expected projectile spill proves that some content crossing the playfield boundary is intentional, so a global crop conclusion would be premature.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Capture the source drawmap, both MCD212 planes, composed hardware raster/aperture, and frontend output at the same gameplay frame. The first stage missing the HUD pixels identifies whether this is source drawing, transfer, clipping, composition, or presentation.

manual_verification.notes: The lower HUD pixels are missing in current gameplay. Windowboxing, the bottom black bar, the elevated HUD position, and projectile spill are retained as expected behavior from the real-hardware reference.
